uncited: This family defines the forward pass that synthesizes a 2D image pixel color from a 3D implicit scene representation by integrating radiance along camera rays.

It sets itself apart from sibling methods like [NeRF Evaluation and Metric Calculation](3079-nerf-evaluation-and-metric-calculation.md) by focusing strictly on the geometric integration and compositing logic rather than loss computation or metric evaluation.
The core mathematical formulation relies on the Beer-Lambert law to convert volume density $\sigma$ into opacity $\alpha$ and transmittance $T$.
*   $N$ is the number of samples along the ray.
*   $\sigma_i$ is the volume density at sample $i$.
*   $c_i$ is the emitted color at sample $i$.
*   $\delta_i$ is the distance between sample $i$ and $i+1$.
To prevent NaNs during gradient computation, a small epsilon $\epsilon$ (typically $10^{-10}$) is added to $(1 - \alpha_j)$ before the cumulative product or exponential calculation .
where $w_i = \alpha_i T_i$ is the weight of sample $i$ .
where $t_i$ is the distance of sample $i$ from the camera origin .
This variant extends the standard forward pass by incorporating alpha masking and NDC (Normalized Device Coordinates) ray sampling.

The final RGB map is computed by weighting RGB values by these alpha weights. This procedure corresponds to discretizing the medium interaction interval into steps and accumulating emission (RGB values) weighted by transmittance/opacity factors, which aligns with the claim.
